rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「中尉。イタリア人たちは、この黄金のことを、本土へ報告しないことを望んでいます」
en: “Lieutenant. The Italians don't want the mainland informed about this gold.”
rows.enText: “Lieutenant. The Italians don't want the mainland informed about this gold.”
rows.jaText: 「中尉。イタリア人たちは、この黄金のことを、本土へ報告しないことを望んでいます」

ja: 「………ふふん。我が国に横領されたくないからであろうな」
en: “...Hmph. They don't want our country taking it for itself, I suppose.”
rows.enText: “...Hmph. They don't want our country taking it for itself, I suppose.”
rows.jaText: 「………ふふん。我が国に横領されたくないからであろうな」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『彼は何と？』
en: “What did he say?”
rows.enText: “What did he say?”
rows.jaText: 『彼は何と？』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『日本が黄金を横領するのを恐れているから、報告されたくないのだろうと言っている』
en: “He says you don't want it reported because you're afraid Japan will appropriate the gold,” I tell her in English.
rows.enText: “He says you don't want it reported because you're afraid Japan will appropriate the gold,” I tell her in English.
rows.jaText: 『日本が黄金を横領するのを恐れているから、報告されたくないのだろうと言っている』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『少尉はむしろ、イタリア本国に知られることを恐れているわ。私たちにとって、今の祖国は連合国の傀儡政権。彼らに知られれば、黄金は返還することになる。しかしそれは、私たちの敵に黄金を渡すようなもの』
en: “The sub-lieutenant is more afraid of the Italian government finding out. As we see it, the government back home is now a puppet of the Allies. If they learn about it, we'll have to return the gold. But that would be giving it to our enemies.”
rows.enText: “The sub-lieutenant is more afraid of the Italian government finding out. As we see it, the government back home is now a puppet of the Allies. If they learn about it, we'll have to return the gold. But that would be giving it to our enemies.”
rows.jaText: 『少尉はむしろ、イタリア本国に知られることを恐れているわ。私たちにとって、今の祖国は連合国の傀儡政権。彼らに知られれば、黄金は返還することになる。しかしそれは、私たちの敵に黄金を渡すようなもの』

ja: 敵の手に黄金を渡さないために、彼らはここまでやって来たのだ。彼らの真の祖国が復興する日まで、この黄金を傀儡の祖国の手から、彼らは隠さなくてはならない…。
en:
They have come all this way to keep the gold out of enemy hands.

Until their true homeland rises again, they must keep it hidden from their puppet homeland...
rows.enText: They have come all this way to keep the gold out of enemy hands. Until their true homeland rises again, they must keep it hidden from their puppet homeland...
rows.jaText: 敵の手に黄金を渡さないために、彼らはここまでやって来たのだ。彼らの真の祖国が復興する日まで、この黄金を傀儡の祖国の手から、彼らは隠さなくてはならない…。

ja: 「右代宮。イタリア人たちに提案せよ。我々は協力を申し出たいとな」
en: “Ushiromiya. Make the Italians a proposal. Tell them we wish to offer our cooperation.”
rows.enText: “Ushiromiya. Make the Italians a proposal. Tell them we wish to offer our cooperation.”
rows.jaText: 「右代宮。イタリア人たちに提案せよ。我々は協力を申し出たいとな」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「協力とは…？」
en: “Cooperation...?”
rows.enText: “Cooperation...?”
rows.jaText: 「協力とは…？」

ja: 「イタリア人たちの言い分はこうであろう？　彼らはその黄金を、祖国に知られることなく隠したいわけだ。しかし、この島から運び出そうとすれば、輸送船を手配せねばならなくなる。そうすれば、本土に知られ、さらにはイタリア本国にも知られることとなる」
en: “This is what the Italians are saying, isn't it? They want to hide the gold without their homeland learning about it. But to move it off this island, they would need to arrange a transport ship. Then the mainland would find out, and so would the government in Italy.”
rows.enText: “This is what the Italians are saying, isn't it? They want to hide the gold without their homeland learning about it. But to move it off this island, they would need to arrange a transport ship. Then the mainland would find out, and so would the government in Italy.”
rows.jaText: 「イタリア人たちの言い分はこうであろう？　彼らはその黄金を、祖国に知られることなく隠したいわけだ。しかし、この島から運び出そうとすれば、輸送船を手配せねばならなくなる。そうすれば、本土に知られ、さらにはイタリア本国にも知られることとなる」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「そうなります。……つまり、あの黄金は、もう六軒島からは運び出せない」
en: “Yes, sir. ...In other words, that gold can no longer leave Rokkenjima.”
rows.enText: “Yes, sir. ...In other words, that gold can no longer leave Rokkenjima.”
rows.jaText: 「そうなります。……つまり、あの黄金は、もう六軒島からは運び出せない」

ja: 彼らの任務は恐らく、祖国再興の日まで、あの黄金を極秘の場所に隠すことだったに違いない。ドイツでも、降伏直前にその隠し財産を、南米などの某所に極秘で運搬して隠した、などという噂がまことしやかに流れる。それは妥当な想像だった。唯一の極秘輸送手段であった潜水艦は完全に航行不能で、浸水は止められず、近い内に完全に沈没するだろう。黄金を極秘に輸送する手段は、もはや存在しないのだ。それはつまり、彼らの任務がこの極東の地で、失敗に終わったことを示していた。その上で、山本中尉は何の協力を申し出ようと言うのか……。
en:
Their mission was probably to conceal it somewhere secret until their homeland could be restored.

There are also plausible-sounding rumors of Germany secretly transporting its hidden wealth to places in South America just before surrendering. It is a reasonable supposition.

The submarine, their only means of transporting it in secret, is completely unseaworthy. The flooding cannot be stopped. Soon it will sink entirely.

They have no way left to move the gold in secret.

Which means their mission has ended in failure here in the Far East.

In that case, what cooperation does Lieutenant Yamamoto intend to offer...?
rows.enText: Their mission was probably to conceal it somewhere secret until their homeland could be restored. There are also plausible-sounding rumors of Germany secretly transporting its hidden wealth to places in South America just before surrendering. It is a reasonable supposition. The submarine, their only means of transporting it in secret, is completely unseaworthy. The flooding cannot be stopped. Soon it will sink entirely. They have no way left to move the gold in secret. Which means their mission has ended in failure here in the Far East. In that case, what cooperation does Lieutenant Yamamoto intend to offer...?
rows.jaText: 彼らの任務は恐らく、祖国再興の日まで、あの黄金を極秘の場所に隠すことだったに違いない。ドイツでも、降伏直前にその隠し財産を、南米などの某所に極秘で運搬して隠した、などという噂がまことしやかに流れる。それは妥当な想像だった。唯一の極秘輸送手段であった潜水艦は完全に航行不能で、浸水は止められず、近い内に完全に沈没するだろう。黄金を極秘に輸送する手段は、もはや存在しないのだ。それはつまり、彼らの任務がこの極東の地で、失敗に終わったことを示していた。その上で、山本中尉は何の協力を申し出ようと言うのか……。

ja: 「この六軒島基地は、誰も知らぬ秘密基地だ。近隣の島民たちは、この島を不吉な無人島と信じて近寄りもしない。……言っている意味がわかるか、右代宮」
en: “This Rokkenjima base is a secret known to no one. The islanders nearby believe this is an unlucky, uninhabited island and won't come near it. ...Do you understand what I'm saying, Ushiromiya?”
rows.enText: “This Rokkenjima base is a secret known to no one. The islanders nearby believe this is an unlucky, uninhabited island and won't come near it. ...Do you understand what I'm saying, Ushiromiya?”
rows.jaText: 「この六軒島基地は、誰も知らぬ秘密基地だ。近隣の島民たちは、この島を不吉な無人島と信じて近寄りもしない。……言っている意味がわかるか、右代宮」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『彼は何と？』
en: “What did he say?”
rows.enText: “What did he say?”
rows.jaText: 『彼は何と？』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『前にも話した通り、この六軒島基地は誰にも知られていない。見ての通り、戦略価値は何もなく、上層部にもすでに忘れられてる。……中尉は、この島に黄金を隠してはどうかと提案したいみたいだ』
en: “As I told you before, no one knows about this base. You can see it has no strategic value. Even the higher command has forgotten us. ...I think the lieutenant wants to suggest hiding the gold on this island.”
rows.enText: “As I told you before, no one knows about this base. You can see it has no strategic value. Even the higher command has forgotten us. ...I think the lieutenant wants to suggest hiding the gold on this island.”
rows.jaText: 『前にも話した通り、この六軒島基地は誰にも知られていない。見ての通り、戦略価値は何もなく、上層部にもすでに忘れられてる。……中尉は、この島に黄金を隠してはどうかと提案したいみたいだ』

ja: ベアトリーチェはすぐにそれを翻訳し、アンジェロ少尉に伝える。少尉は下士官たちと早口に議論を始める。表情は苦々しい。同盟国とはいえ、祖国再建の大切な黄金を、東洋人の手に委ねたくはないのだろう。しかし、選択の余地が残されているとは思えない。
en:
Beatrice immediately translates for Sub-Lieutenant Angelo.

He and the NCOs begin a rapid discussion. Their expressions are bitter.

Even as allies, they probably do not want to entrust gold so vital to rebuilding their homeland to Asians. But I cannot see what choice they have left.
rows.enText: Beatrice immediately translates for Sub-Lieutenant Angelo. He and the NCOs begin a rapid discussion. Their expressions are bitter. Even as allies, they probably do not want to entrust gold so vital to rebuilding their homeland to Asians. But I cannot see what choice they have left.
rows.jaText: ベアトリーチェはすぐにそれを翻訳し、アンジェロ少尉に伝える。少尉は下士官たちと早口に議論を始める。表情は苦々しい。同盟国とはいえ、祖国再建の大切な黄金を、東洋人の手に委ねたくはないのだろう。しかし、選択の余地が残されているとは思えない。

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『……激しく議論しているわ。他に手はないと言う者もいるし、それでも祖国に忠誠を尽くすべきだと言う者もいる。……少尉は板挟みになってるわ』
en: “...They're arguing fiercely. Some say there's no other way. Others say they must remain loyal to their homeland regardless. ...The sub-lieutenant is caught in the middle.”
rows.enText: “...They're arguing fiercely. Some say there's no other way. Others say they must remain loyal to their homeland regardless. ...The sub-lieutenant is caught in the middle.”
rows.jaText: 『……激しく議論しているわ。他に手はないと言う者もいるし、それでも祖国に忠誠を尽くすべきだと言う者もいる。……少尉は板挟みになってるわ』

ja:
黄金隠匿は、滅んだ祖国の最後の命令だ。
しかしその命令はもはや遂行不能だ。本土や祖国に知られれば、彼らの望まぬ人間たちに接収されることになる。彼らが祖国の命令を忠実に実行しようとするなら、………山本中尉の、この島に隠せばいいという提案は、極めて妥当なものだ…。
en:
Concealing the gold was the last order of their fallen homeland.

But they can no longer carry it out. If the mainland or their homeland learns about it, it will be confiscated by the very people they wish to keep it from.

If they mean to obey their homeland's orders faithfully, ...Lieutenant Yamamoto's proposal to hide it on this island is eminently reasonable...
rows.enText: Concealing the gold was the last order of their fallen homeland. But they can no longer carry it out. If the mainland or their homeland learns about it, it will be confiscated by the very people they wish to keep it from. If they mean to obey their homeland's orders faithfully, ...Lieutenant Yamamoto's proposal to hide it on this island is eminently reasonable...
rows.jaText:
黄金隠匿は、滅んだ祖国の最後の命令だ。
しかしその命令はもはや遂行不能だ。本土や祖国に知られれば、彼らの望まぬ人間たちに接収されることになる。彼らが祖国の命令を忠実に実行しようとするなら、………山本中尉の、この島に隠せばいいという提案は、極めて妥当なものだ…。

ja: たとえ言葉が理解できなくても、彼らが悩んでいることは、山本中尉にもわかっているようだった。
en: Even without understanding the language, Lieutenant Yamamoto seems to recognize their predicament.
rows.enText: Even without understanding the language, Lieutenant Yamamoto seems to recognize their predicament.
rows.jaText: たとえ言葉が理解できなくても、彼らが悩んでいることは、山本中尉にもわかっているようだった。

ja: 「くっくっく、我々が協力すれば、あの黄金を厳重に隠すことが出来るぞ。幸いなことに、廃棄された地下壕が長々と、この島の地下を横断している」
en: “Heh heh heh. With our cooperation, you can keep that gold well hidden. Fortunately, abandoned underground tunnels run a long way across this island.”
rows.enText: “Heh heh heh. With our cooperation, you can keep that gold well hidden. Fortunately, abandoned underground tunnels run a long way across this island.”
rows.jaText: 「くっくっく、我々が協力すれば、あの黄金を厳重に隠すことが出来るぞ。幸いなことに、廃棄された地下壕が長々と、この島の地下を横断している」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『……この島の地下に黄金を隠して埋めれば、誰にも発見できないと言ってる』
en: “...He says that if you hide the gold by burying it under the island, no one will find it.”
rows.enText: “...He says that if you hide the gold by burying it under the island, no one will find it.”
rows.jaText: 『……この島の地下に黄金を隠して埋めれば、誰にも発見できないと言ってる』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『現実的な申し出だと議論してるわ。……でも、日本人の手を借りるのに、抵抗を感じてるみたい』
en: “They're discussing it as a practical offer. ...But they seem reluctant to accept help from the Japanese.”
rows.enText: “They're discussing it as a practical offer. ...But they seem reluctant to accept help from the Japanese.”
rows.jaText: 『現実的な申し出だと議論してるわ。……でも、日本人の手を借りるのに、抵抗を感じてるみたい』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「……議論が難航しているようです」
en: “...Their discussion seems to be going badly.”
rows.enText: “...Their discussion seems to be going badly.”
rows.jaText: 「……議論が難航しているようです」

ja: 「くっくっく。議論の余地などあるのか、イタリア人。我々の協力なくば、あの黄金は隠せんぞ？　まさか、いつまでも波打ち際に積み上げて置く訳にも行くまい？」
en: “Heh heh heh. Is there anything to discuss, Italians? Without our cooperation, you can't hide that gold. Surely you can't leave it piled up at the water's edge forever?”
rows.enText: “Heh heh heh. Is there anything to discuss, Italians? Without our cooperation, you can't hide that gold. Surely you can't leave it piled up at the water's edge forever?”
rows.jaText: 「くっくっく。議論の余地などあるのか、イタリア人。我々の協力なくば、あの黄金は隠せんぞ？　まさか、いつまでも波打ち際に積み上げて置く訳にも行くまい？」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『アンジェロ少尉は、黄金のことを知る人間を最小で抑えたいみたい。……日本人は信用できないけど、山本中尉の申し出が、今は最善と見てるみたいよ。でも、訝しがってるわ』
en: “The sub-lieutenant wants to keep the number of people who know about it as small as possible. ...He doesn't trust the Japanese, but thinks your lieutenant's proposal is the best option for now. Still, he's suspicious.”
rows.enText: “The sub-lieutenant wants to keep the number of people who know about it as small as possible. ...He doesn't trust the Japanese, but thinks your lieutenant's proposal is the best option for now. Still, he's suspicious.”
rows.jaText: 『アンジェロ少尉は、黄金のことを知る人間を最小で抑えたいみたい。……日本人は信用できないけど、山本中尉の申し出が、今は最善と見てるみたいよ。でも、訝しがってるわ』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『何を？』
en: “Of what?”
rows.enText: “Of what?”
rows.jaText: 『何を？』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『１０ｔの黄金を隠すという労力の提供と守秘義務を、彼らが本当に無償で提供してくれるのかと、ね……』
en: “Of whether they'll really supply the labor to hide ten tons of gold, and keep it secret, for nothing...”
rows.enText: “Of whether they'll really supply the labor to hide ten tons of gold, and keep it secret, for nothing...”
rows.jaText: 『１０ｔの黄金を隠すという労力の提供と守秘義務を、彼らが本当に無償で提供してくれるのかと、ね……』

ja: 「五分と五分だ」
en: “Half and half.”
rows.enText: “Half and half.”
rows.jaText: 「五分と五分だ」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「……中尉、それはまさか、」
en: “...Lieutenant, you don't mean—”
rows.enText: “...Lieutenant, you don't mean—”
rows.jaText: 「……中尉、それはまさか、」

ja: 「あの黄金の半分を我々に寄越せ。それを手間賃に、残りの半分を厳重に隠してやろう」
en: “Give us half that gold. For that fee, we'll make certain the other half is securely hidden.”
rows.enText: “Give us half that gold. For that fee, we'll make certain the other half is securely hidden.”
rows.jaText: 「あの黄金の半分を我々に寄越せ。それを手間賃に、残りの半分を厳重に隠してやろう」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『……は、半分を寄越せと言ってる』
en: “...He—he says he wants half.”
rows.enText: “...He—he says he wants half.”
rows.jaText: 『……は、半分を寄越せと言ってる』

ja: ベアトリーチェがそれを通訳した途端、アンジェロ少尉はバンと机を叩いて立ち上がる。山本中尉は、乱暴者と恐れられていたと自ら言うだけあり、気圧された様子もなく、……いやむしろ、さっきより余裕をもって言う。
en:
The instant Beatrice translates that, Sub-Lieutenant Angelo slams the table and gets to his feet.

Lieutenant Yamamoto boasts that people fear him for his brutality, and he is not the least intimidated. ...If anything, he speaks with greater ease than before.
rows.enText: The instant Beatrice translates that, Sub-Lieutenant Angelo slams the table and gets to his feet. Lieutenant Yamamoto boasts that people fear him for his brutality, and he is not the least intimidated. ...If anything, he speaks with greater ease than before.
rows.jaText: ベアトリーチェがそれを通訳した途端、アンジェロ少尉はバンと机を叩いて立ち上がる。山本中尉は、乱暴者と恐れられていたと自ら言うだけあり、気圧された様子もなく、……いやむしろ、さっきより余裕をもって言う。

ja: 「本来なら断りようのない話だ。８割を要求してもおかしくない。それを、敬意を表して五分と五分にしようと提案しているのだ」「……これは我々だけに優位な話ではない。イタリア人たちが外部にこのことを漏らせば、全ての黄金は日本かイタリアに接収されるだろう。我々には１円たりとも転がり込んで来ない。我々は全員が共犯でなくてはならないのだ」
en:
“You are hardly in a position to refuse. I could quite reasonably demand eighty percent. Out of respect, I am proposing an equal split.”

“...This arrangement doesn't favor only us. If the Italians tell anyone outside, all the gold will be confiscated by Japan or Italy. We won't see a single yen. We must all be accomplices.”
rows.enText: “You are hardly in a position to refuse. I could quite reasonably demand eighty percent. Out of respect, I am proposing an equal split.” “...This arrangement doesn't favor only us. If the Italians tell anyone outside, all the gold will be confiscated by Japan or Italy. We won't see a single yen. We must all be accomplices.”
rows.jaText: 「本来なら断りようのない話だ。８割を要求してもおかしくない。それを、敬意を表して五分と五分にしようと提案しているのだ」「……これは我々だけに優位な話ではない。イタリア人たちが外部にこのことを漏らせば、全ての黄金は日本かイタリアに接収されるだろう。我々には１円たりとも転がり込んで来ない。我々は全員が共犯でなくてはならないのだ」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『全員に着服の共犯になれと言ってる。……中尉はすでに軍人としてでなく、個人として話をしている…』
en: “He says we should all become accomplices in embezzling it. ...He's no longer speaking as a military officer, but as a private individual...”
rows.enText: “He says we should all become accomplices in embezzling it. ...He's no longer speaking as a military officer, but as a private individual...”
rows.jaText: 『全員に着服の共犯になれと言ってる。……中尉はすでに軍人としてでなく、個人として話をしている…』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『何てこと……。黄金に目が眩んだのね…』
en: “Good God... The gold has blinded him...”
rows.enText: “Good God... The gold has blinded him...”
rows.jaText: 『何てこと……。黄金に目が眩んだのね…』

ja: 山本中尉はにやにやと笑う。ベアトリーチェの言う通り、その目は黄金に眩んでいるようだった…。
en:
Lieutenant Yamamoto grins.

Just as Beatrice says, his eyes seem blinded by the gold...
rows.enText: Lieutenant Yamamoto grins. Just as Beatrice says, his eyes seem blinded by the gold...
rows.jaText: 山本中尉はにやにやと笑う。ベアトリーチェの言う通り、その目は黄金に眩んでいるようだった…。

ja: 「あのまま山積みにしていれば、やがて本土から来る迎えの連中の目に、否応なく入るだろう。そうなれば、ここにいる誰もが得をしないぞ。我々の申し出を受けて、早急に黄金を隠すべきだ」
en: “Leave it piled up like that, and sooner or later the men coming from the mainland to collect you are bound to see it. Then no one here gains anything. You should accept our offer and hide the gold at once.”
rows.enText: “Leave it piled up like that, and sooner or later the men coming from the mainland to collect you are bound to see it. Then no one here gains anything. You should accept our offer and hide the gold at once.”
rows.jaText: 「あのまま山積みにしていれば、やがて本土から来る迎えの連中の目に、否応なく入るだろう。そうなれば、ここにいる誰もが得をしないぞ。我々の申し出を受けて、早急に黄金を隠すべきだ」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『……アンジェロ少尉は、日本政府やイタリア政府にはどうしても知られたくないみたい。彼は自分が与えられた任務に、最後まで責任を持ちたいみたいよ』
en: “...The sub-lieutenant seems determined that neither the Japanese nor the Italian government should learn about it. He seems determined to see his mission through to the very end.”
rows.enText: “...The sub-lieutenant seems determined that neither the Japanese nor the Italian government should learn about it. He seems determined to see his mission through to the very end.”
rows.jaText: 『……アンジェロ少尉は、日本政府やイタリア政府にはどうしても知られたくないみたい。彼は自分が与えられた任務に、最後まで責任を持ちたいみたいよ』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『つまりどういうことだ？』
en: “What does that mean?”
rows.enText: “What does that mean?”
rows.jaText: 『つまりどういうことだ？』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『何割かを口止め料として与えてでも、島内に地中深く埋めることを望んでるわ。……もちろん、下士官たちには異論もあるみたい。５割は問題外だと憤慨してるわ』
en: “He wants it buried deep on this island, even if he has to give some away to buy their silence. ...Of course, the NCOs don't seem to agree. They're furious. Fifty percent is out of the question.”
rows.enText: “He wants it buried deep on this island, even if he has to give some away to buy their silence. ...Of course, the NCOs don't seem to agree. They're furious. Fifty percent is out of the question.”
rows.jaText: 『何割かを口止め料として与えてでも、島内に地中深く埋めることを望んでるわ。……もちろん、下士官たちには異論もあるみたい。５割は問題外だと憤慨してるわ』

ja: 「右代宮。イタリア人たちの感触はどうだ？」
en: “Ushiromiya. How do the Italians feel?”
rows.enText: “Ushiromiya. How do the Italians feel?”
rows.jaText: 「右代宮。イタリア人たちの感触はどうだ？」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「………彼らも黄金が、これ以上の人目につくことを望んでいないようです。……しかし、取り分に異論があるようです」
en: “...They don't seem to want any more people to see the gold either. ...But they object to the share.”
rows.enText: “...They don't seem to want any more people to see the gold either. ...But they object to the share.”
rows.jaText: 「………彼らも黄金が、これ以上の人目につくことを望んでいないようです。……しかし、取り分に異論があるようです」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『少尉は、１割ならば検討できると言ってるわ。……無論、山本中尉がそれで納得しないだろうとも言ってるけど』
en: “The sub-lieutenant says he could consider ten percent. ...Though of course, he says your lieutenant probably won't accept it.”
rows.enText: “The sub-lieutenant says he could consider ten percent. ...Though of course, he says your lieutenant probably won't accept it.”
rows.jaText: 『少尉は、１割ならば検討できると言ってるわ。……無論、山本中尉がそれで納得しないだろうとも言ってるけど』

ja: 「右代宮。イタリア人の返事は如何に？」
en: “Ushiromiya. What is their answer?”
rows.enText: “Ushiromiya. What is their answer?”
rows.jaText: 「右代宮。イタリア人の返事は如何に？」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「……１割なら検討すると」
en: “...They would consider ten percent.”
rows.enText: “...They would consider ten percent.”
rows.jaText: 「……１割なら検討すると」

ja: 今度は山本中尉が激しく机を叩く。しかし、イタリア人たちも気圧されはしない。……狭い室内を、火薬の臭いのする緊迫感が満たしていく…。
en:
Now Lieutenant Yamamoto slams the table. But the Italians are not intimidated either.

...The cramped room fills with tension that reeks of gunpowder...
rows.enText: Now Lieutenant Yamamoto slams the table. But the Italians are not intimidated either. ...The cramped room fills with tension that reeks of gunpowder...
rows.jaText: 今度は山本中尉が激しく机を叩く。しかし、イタリア人たちも気圧されはしない。……狭い室内を、火薬の臭いのする緊迫感が満たしていく…。

ja: しかし、その乱暴な仕草とは裏腹に、やはり山本中尉の表情は不敵で余裕あるものだった。交渉のイニシアチブは自分にあるのだという、自信があるのだろう。
en: Despite the violent gesture, the lieutenant's expression remains defiant and untroubled. He must be confident that he controls the negotiation.
rows.enText: Despite the violent gesture, the lieutenant's expression remains defiant and untroubled. He must be confident that he controls the negotiation.
rows.jaText: しかし、その乱暴な仕草とは裏腹に、やはり山本中尉の表情は不敵で余裕あるものだった。交渉のイニシアチブは自分にあるのだという、自信があるのだろう。

ja: 「１割！　１割か、それは慎ましやかな提案だ。……いいだろう、なら１割を譲ってやろう。四分六だ。これ以上は譲らんと伝えろ！」
en: “Ten percent! Ten percent, is it? A very modest proposal. ...Very well. I'll concede ten percent. Forty-sixty. Tell them that's my final offer!”
rows.enText: “Ten percent! Ten percent, is it? A very modest proposal. ...Very well. I'll concede ten percent. Forty-sixty. Tell them that's my final offer!”
rows.jaText: 「１割！　１割か、それは慎ましやかな提案だ。……いいだろう、なら１割を譲ってやろう。四分六だ。これ以上は譲らんと伝えろ！」

ja: 日本側４割。イタリア側６割。中尉は強気に出ているが、実際は決して互角の交渉ではない。イタリア人たちが、自分たちもこの黄金を横領しようという考えでいるなら、大した問題ではない。しかしもし。彼らが高潔な愛国者であり、……たとえ滅んだ傀儡の祖国であっても、再建のために黄金を返還すべきだという結論に至った場合。彼らはむしろ逆に、黄金の存在をイタリア大使館員に告白するだろう。イタリア政府はやがて連合国を通じてそれの返還を求める。……全てがイタリアには戻らないだろうが、荒れ果てた街並みの再建に、その黄金は有効に利用されるかもしれない。そうなれば山本中尉たちは、せいぜい数本のインゴットを誤魔化せるかどうかだ。欲深な彼は、この島を自分たちだけの宝島にして、巨万の富を独り占めしようと企んでいるのだ。……その野望のためには、イタリア人たちが黄金のことを、秘匿しなくてはならない。
en:
Forty percent for the Japanese. Sixty for the Italians.

The lieutenant is taking a hard line, but the negotiation is by no means on equal terms.

If the Italians intend to embezzle this gold themselves, there is no great problem.

But suppose they are honorable patriots. Suppose they decide that even if their homeland has fallen and become a puppet state, the gold should be returned to rebuild it.

Then they will do precisely the opposite: confess its existence to the Italian embassy staff.

The Italian government will eventually demand its return through the Allies. ...Not all of it will make its way back to Italy, but perhaps it can be put to good use rebuilding the devastated streets.

In that event, Yamamoto and his men would be lucky to get away with a few ingots.

In his greed, he means to turn this island into their own treasure island and keep that colossal fortune for themselves.

...For that ambition to succeed, the Italians must keep the gold a secret.
rows.enText: Forty percent for the Japanese. Sixty for the Italians. The lieutenant is taking a hard line, but the negotiation is by no means on equal terms. If the Italians intend to embezzle this gold themselves, there is no great problem. But suppose they are honorable patriots. Suppose they decide that even if their homeland has fallen and become a puppet state, the gold should be returned to rebuild it. Then they will do precisely the opposite: confess its existence to the Italian embassy staff. The Italian government will eventually demand its return through the Allies. ...Not all of it will make its way back to Italy, but perhaps it can be put to good use rebuilding the devastated streets. In that event, Yamamoto and his men would be lucky to get away with a few ingots. In his greed, he means to turn this island into their own treasure island and keep that colossal fortune for themselves. ...For that ambition to succeed, the Italians must keep the gold a secret.
rows.jaText: 日本側４割。イタリア側６割。中尉は強気に出ているが、実際は決して互角の交渉ではない。イタリア人たちが、自分たちもこの黄金を横領しようという考えでいるなら、大した問題ではない。しかしもし。彼らが高潔な愛国者であり、……たとえ滅んだ傀儡の祖国であっても、再建のために黄金を返還すべきだという結論に至った場合。彼らはむしろ逆に、黄金の存在をイタリア大使館員に告白するだろう。イタリア政府はやがて連合国を通じてそれの返還を求める。……全てがイタリアには戻らないだろうが、荒れ果てた街並みの再建に、その黄金は有効に利用されるかもしれない。そうなれば山本中尉たちは、せいぜい数本のインゴットを誤魔化せるかどうかだ。欲深な彼は、この島を自分たちだけの宝島にして、巨万の富を独り占めしようと企んでいるのだ。……その野望のためには、イタリア人たちが黄金のことを、秘匿しなくてはならない。

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『しかし疑問だ。………アンジェロ少尉が誰にも黄金を渡したくないなら、沈み行く潜水艦に任せて沈めれば良かったはず。どうして荷揚げを？』
en: “There's something I don't understand. ...If Sub-Lieutenant Angelo doesn't want anyone to have the gold, he could have let it go down with the sinking submarine. Why unload it?”
rows.enText: “There's something I don't understand. ...If Sub-Lieutenant Angelo doesn't want anyone to have the gold, he could have let it go down with the sinking submarine. Why unload it?”
rows.jaText: 『しかし疑問だ。………アンジェロ少尉が誰にも黄金を渡したくないなら、沈み行く潜水艦に任せて沈めれば良かったはず。どうして荷揚げを？』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『……考えたくはないけれど。……命令が遂行不能になった時点で、少尉はこの黄金を横領することを考え始めたのかも。彼は今、下士官たちに、軍人としての意見と、祖国に家族が待つ一個人としての意見を聞きたいと言っているわ。……堅物の下士官たちが激高してる』
en: “...I don't want to believe it. ...But perhaps, when the mission became impossible, he began considering embezzling it. He's asking the NCOs now for their opinions both as servicemen and as individuals with families waiting at home. ...The hard-liners are furious.”
rows.enText: “...I don't want to believe it. ...But perhaps, when the mission became impossible, he began considering embezzling it. He's asking the NCOs now for their opinions both as servicemen and as individuals with families waiting at home. ...The hard-liners are furious.”
rows.jaText: 『……考えたくはないけれど。……命令が遂行不能になった時点で、少尉はこの黄金を横領することを考え始めたのかも。彼は今、下士官たちに、軍人としての意見と、祖国に家族が待つ一個人としての意見を聞きたいと言っているわ。……堅物の下士官たちが激高してる』

ja: イタリア人たちは、感情的になりながら激しい議論を交わし出す。滅んだとはいえ、祖国の命令にひたすら従い、ここまでやって来たのだ。このような任務に当てられるのだから、彼らは特に忠誠心が高い兵士たちだろう。異国人に着服と山分けを唆され、素直に首を縦に振れるわけではなさそうだ……。アンジェロ少尉は下士官たちの想像以上の激高に、なだめるのが精一杯のように見える。……やはり、黄金は彼らをも惑わせているのだ。誰もが、本音と建前を交錯し、どうすればいいのか戸惑っている……。
en:
The Italians begin a fierce, emotional argument.

Though their homeland has fallen, they have obeyed its orders single-mindedly all the way here. Men assigned a mission like this are probably especially loyal.

They hardly seem ready to agree when foreigners urge them to embezzle the gold and divide it...

Their fury seems greater than Sub-Lieutenant Angelo expected. He can barely keep them calm.

...The gold is bewildering them too.

Private feelings and public principles cross and tangle. No one knows what to do...
rows.enText: The Italians begin a fierce, emotional argument. Though their homeland has fallen, they have obeyed its orders single-mindedly all the way here. Men assigned a mission like this are probably especially loyal. They hardly seem ready to agree when foreigners urge them to embezzle the gold and divide it... Their fury seems greater than Sub-Lieutenant Angelo expected. He can barely keep them calm. ...The gold is bewildering them too. Private feelings and public principles cross and tangle. No one knows what to do...
rows.jaText: イタリア人たちは、感情的になりながら激しい議論を交わし出す。滅んだとはいえ、祖国の命令にひたすら従い、ここまでやって来たのだ。このような任務に当てられるのだから、彼らは特に忠誠心が高い兵士たちだろう。異国人に着服と山分けを唆され、素直に首を縦に振れるわけではなさそうだ……。アンジェロ少尉は下士官たちの想像以上の激高に、なだめるのが精一杯のように見える。……やはり、黄金は彼らをも惑わせているのだ。誰もが、本音と建前を交錯し、どうすればいいのか戸惑っている……。

ja: 「ヤツらの返答は如何に？！　右代宮ッ！！」
en: “What is their answer?! Ushiromiya!!”
rows.enText: “What is their answer?! Ushiromiya!!”
rows.jaText: 「ヤツらの返答は如何に？！　右代宮ッ！！」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『……ビーチェ。中尉が返事を求めてる』
en: “...Bice. The lieutenant wants an answer.”
rows.enText: “...Bice. The lieutenant wants an answer.”
rows.jaText: 『……ビーチェ。中尉が返事を求めてる』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『………考える時間がほしいと言ってるわ。私はあなたと話せたから、気が紛れて良かったけれど、他の人たちはそうじゃないの』『……とても長い航海の果てに、大勢の仲間を失って、極限状態でここにいるわ。唯一の心の拠り所だった任務ももはや喪失してる。どうすればいいのか、彼らもわかってないの…』
en:
“...They say they need time to think. Talking to you helped take my mind off things, but the others haven't had that.

“...They've endured a very long voyage and lost so many comrades. They're at the breaking point. Even their mission, the one thing they could hold on to, is gone now. They don't know what to do...”
rows.enText: “...They say they need time to think. Talking to you helped take my mind off things, but the others haven't had that. “...They've endured a very long voyage and lost so many comrades. They're at the breaking point. Even their mission, the one thing they could hold on to, is gone now. They don't know what to do...”
rows.jaText: 『………考える時間がほしいと言ってるわ。私はあなたと話せたから、気が紛れて良かったけれど、他の人たちはそうじゃないの』『……とても長い航海の果てに、大勢の仲間を失って、極限状態でここにいるわ。唯一の心の拠り所だった任務ももはや喪失してる。どうすればいいのか、彼らもわかってないの…』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「中尉。……彼らは時間が欲しいと言っています」
en: “Lieutenant. ...They say they need time.”
rows.enText: “Lieutenant. ...They say they need time.”
rows.jaText: 「中尉。……彼らは時間が欲しいと言っています」

ja: 「くっくっく、いいとも、大いに議論したらいい。しかし時間はないぞ。隠すとなったら、時間と手間がかかる。……明日の正午までに結論しろ。以上だ、イタリア人ども！」
en: “Heh heh heh. Certainly. Discuss it all you like. But there isn't much time. Concealing it will take time and labor. ...I want your decision by noon tomorrow. That is all, Italians!”
rows.enText: “Heh heh heh. Certainly. Discuss it all you like. But there isn't much time. Concealing it will take time and labor. ...I want your decision by noon tomorrow. That is all, Italians!”
rows.jaText: 「くっくっく、いいとも、大いに議論したらいい。しかし時間はないぞ。隠すとなったら、時間と手間がかかる。……明日の正午までに結論しろ。以上だ、イタリア人ども！」

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『……回答期限は明日の正午だそうだ。……中尉め、まるで脅迫だ』
en: “...He says the deadline is noon tomorrow. ...The bastard. It's practically a threat.”
rows.enText: “...He says the deadline is noon tomorrow. ...The bastard. It's practically a threat.”
rows.jaText: 『……回答期限は明日の正午だそうだ。……中尉め、まるで脅迫だ』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『少尉は、全員の意見を聞くと言ってるわ…』
en: “The sub-lieutenant says he'll hear everyone's opinion...”
rows.enText: “The sub-lieutenant says he'll hear everyone's opinion...”
rows.jaText: 『少尉は、全員の意見を聞くと言ってるわ…』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『感触は？』
en: “What do you think will happen?”
rows.enText: “What do you think will happen?”
rows.jaText: 『感触は？』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『多分、難航するわ。……少尉自身は山分けもありえると考えてるみたいだけど、下士官や、他の仲間たちは多分反対するわ。……みんな、この極東までの航海で、大切な仲間を大勢失ってる。彼らは頑なに祖国への忠誠を貫きたがってる』
en: “It'll probably be difficult. ...He seems willing to consider a division, but the NCOs and the others will probably oppose it. ...They've lost so many dear comrades on the voyage to the Far East. They want to hold stubbornly to their loyalty.”
rows.enText: “It'll probably be difficult. ...He seems willing to consider a division, but the NCOs and the others will probably oppose it. ...They've lost so many dear comrades on the voyage to the Far East. They want to hold stubbornly to their loyalty.”
rows.jaText: 『多分、難航するわ。……少尉自身は山分けもありえると考えてるみたいだけど、下士官や、他の仲間たちは多分反対するわ。……みんな、この極東までの航海で、大切な仲間を大勢失ってる。彼らは頑なに祖国への忠誠を貫きたがってる』

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 『……中尉の申し出は断ると？』
en: “...They'll turn the lieutenant down?”
rows.enText: “...They'll turn the lieutenant down?”
rows.jaText: 『……中尉の申し出は断ると？』

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: 『断っても、どうせ黄金は誰かの手に渡るわ。……何も残らないなら、せめてインゴットの１本ずつでも密かに持ち帰ろうという少尉の言い分に、同調者も出そうだけど……。こういう時の男って、勢いだけが迷走するわ。私も見当が付かない…』
en: “Even if they do, someone will get the gold. ...Some might agree with him that if they're going to be left with nothing, they should at least take an ingot each home in secret... At times like this, men let their passion run away with them. I can't tell either...”
rows.enText: “Even if they do, someone will get the gold. ...Some might agree with him that if they're going to be left with nothing, they should at least take an ingot each home in secret... At times like this, men let their passion run away with them. I can't tell either...”
rows.jaText: 『断っても、どうせ黄金は誰かの手に渡るわ。……何も残らないなら、せめてインゴットの１本ずつでも密かに持ち帰ろうという少尉の言い分に、同調者も出そうだけど……。こういう時の男って、勢いだけが迷走するわ。私も見当が付かない…』

rows.speaker: Rion Ushiromiya
ja: 「……イタリア人たちの胸中は、複雑でしょうね」
en: “...The Italians must have had very complicated feelings.”
rows.enText: “...The Italians must have had very complicated feelings.”
rows.jaText: 「……イタリア人たちの胸中は、複雑でしょうね」

rows.speaker: Willard H. Wright
rows.speakerJa: ウィラード・Ｈ・ライト
ja: 「彼らにとって、降伏後のイタリアは敵国同然だろう。黄金をそのイタリアに返還するのは、彼らの長い旅路を全て否定するのと同じだ」
en: “To them, Italy after its surrender would be as good as an enemy nation. Returning the gold there would negate their entire, long voyage.”
rows.enText: “To them, Italy after its surrender would be as good as an enemy nation. Returning the gold there would negate their entire, long voyage.”
rows.jaText: 「彼らにとって、降伏後のイタリアは敵国同然だろう。黄金をそのイタリアに返還するのは、彼らの長い旅路を全て否定するのと同じだ」

rows.speaker: Rion Ushiromiya
ja: 「しかし、黄金を着服して山分けすることも、彼らの旅路の否定になります…」
en: “But embezzling it and dividing it among themselves would negate that voyage too...”
rows.enText: “But embezzling it and dividing it among themselves would negate that voyage too...”
rows.jaText: 「しかし、黄金を着服して山分けすることも、彼らの旅路の否定になります…」

rows.speaker: Willard H. Wright
rows.speakerJa: ウィラード・Ｈ・ライト
ja: 「彼らが義理立てすべき祖国はすでに滅んでる。その時点で、彼らの旅路の意味など、もう失われてる。気の毒な話だ」
en: “The homeland they owe their allegiance to has already fallen. At that point, their voyage has already lost its meaning. A miserable business.”
rows.enText: “The homeland they owe their allegiance to has already fallen. At that point, their voyage has already lost its meaning. A miserable business.”
rows.jaText: 「彼らが義理立てすべき祖国はすでに滅んでる。その時点で、彼らの旅路の意味など、もう失われてる。気の毒な話だ」

rows.speaker: Rion Ushiromiya
ja: 「……どうせ意味のないことなら、インゴットの１本でもありつけた方が、まだマシだと？」
en: “...If it means nothing either way, they'd be better off at least getting an ingot out of it?”
rows.enText: “...If it means nothing either way, they'd be better off at least getting an ingot out of it?”
rows.jaText: 「……どうせ意味のないことなら、インゴットの１本でもありつけた方が、まだマシだと？」

rows.speaker: Willard H. Wright
rows.speakerJa: ウィラード・Ｈ・ライト
ja: 「損得勘定で言えばそうなる。…………そうならねぇのが、男ってもんだがな」
en: “That's how the calculation works. ...But men aren't calculations.”
rows.enText: “That's how the calculation works. ...But men aren't calculations.”
rows.jaText: 「損得勘定で言えばそうなる。…………そうならねぇのが、男ってもんだがな」

ja: 狭い部屋にイタリア人たちが集まり、激論を交わしていた。
en: The Italians have gathered in a small room, arguing furiously in Italian.
rows.enText: The Italians have gathered in a small room, arguing furiously in Italian.
rows.jaText: 狭い部屋にイタリア人たちが集まり、激論を交わしていた。

ja: “反対です！　死んだ戦友たちのためにも、断固、軍人魂を貫くべきです！”“貫くとはどういうことか。この島に黄金を隠せということか。東洋人たちの申し出を受けろということか！”“東洋人たちは信用できません！　特にあのヤマモトという男！　断じて油断できません！”“黄金を荷揚げして日本人たちに見られたのはやはり失敗でした！　艦と共に沈めるべきでした！”“日本人の基地で沈めてどうする？！　やがていつかは引き上げられる。隠したことにはならない！”“いずれにせよ、この島から黄金を誰にも知られずに運び出す方法はない”“洋上で名誉ある自沈を選んでいたらこんなことには…！！”“艦のダメージが致命的だったことが、あの時点でわかっていたら……”“どうしてあの時、少佐は日本軍に救援要請を？　日本軍にこの黄金のことを知られたら、少佐はどう任務を遂行するつもりだったんだ？”“少佐が救援要請を出した時点で、我々の任務はもう、失敗していたんだ！”“諸君にも、祖国で待つ家族がいるはずだ。そして極東の島国まで、よく航海に耐えた。それに対する、これは正当な報酬なのだという、考え方もあるっ”“ざわざわざわ！　ざわざわざわざわ！！”
en:
“I object! For the sake of our dead comrades, we must uphold our honor as soldiers to the end!”

“What does that mean? Conceal the gold on this island? Accept those Asians' offer?”

“We cannot trust them! Especially that man Yamamoto! We must never let our guard down around him!”

“Unloading the gold and letting the Japanese see it was a mistake! We should have sunk it with the boat!”

“What good would sinking it at a Japanese base do?! Sooner or later it would be salvaged. That wouldn't hide it!”

“Whatever we do, there's no way to move it off this island without anyone knowing.”

“If we'd chosen an honorable scuttling out at sea, none of this would have...!”

“If we'd known then that the damage was fatal...”

“Why did the lieutenant commander request assistance from the Japanese? How did he intend to complete the mission if they learned about the gold?”

“The mission had failed the moment he asked for help!”

“You all have families waiting for you at home. You endured the voyage all the way to this island nation in the Far East. There is an argument that this is a fair reward for that!”

The clamor grows. Voices pile upon voices.

“...Corporal. What final measure?”

ja: ごくりと、誰かの喉が鳴る。重苦しい緊張感が部屋を支配する…。
en: Someone swallows audibly. An oppressive tension takes possession of the room...
rows.enText: Someone swallows audibly. An oppressive tension takes possession of the room...

ja: “日本人たちは弛みきっています。実戦経験もない、腰抜けばかりです”“我々は精兵です。すでに基地内の間取りのほぼ全てと、日本人の人数、配置状況は把握しています。少尉の命令があれば、短時間で制圧できるでしょう”“戦闘員と思わしきはヤマモトを含めて数人程度。残りは軍属の作業員風情です。上辺の人数は日本人が上ですが、実質兵力ではこちらが優位です”“日本人を殺せば、迎えの船が来た時、それをどう説明する？　誤魔化しようがないぞ？！”“死体さえ見つからなければ、どうとでも誤魔化せます”“少尉。……この基地を制圧するのは容易です。ヤマモト以下、主要な兵士数人を殺して見せれば、あっさりと作業員たちは降伏するでしょう”“彼らに黄金を運ばせ、地中に埋めましょう。……もちろん、彼らの口は永遠に塞ぎますが”“日本人たちを、皆殺しにするということか……”“殺しましょう。全員殺せば、黄金のことは誰にも知られずに済むのです”
en:
“The Japanese have grown lax. They're all cowards with no combat experience.”

“We are elite soldiers. We already know almost the entire layout of the base, their numbers, and their positions. On your order, we could secure it quickly.”

“Only a few seem to be fighting men, including Yamamoto. The rest are mere civilian laborers. They outnumber us on paper, but we have greater effective strength.”

“If we kill them, how will we explain it when the ship arrives to collect us? There's no way to cover it up!”

“If no bodies are found, we can say anything we like.”

“Sub-Lieutenant. ...It would be easy to take this base. Kill Yamamoto and a few of his key men as an example, and the laborers will surrender readily enough.”

“We'll make them move the gold and bury it. ...Of course, we'll silence them forever afterward.”

“You mean...kill every Japanese man here...”

“Let's kill them. Kill them all, and no one will ever learn about the gold.”

en: At that moment, the supposedly locked door is unlocked. It opens a crack. Something metallic is thrown inside.

en:
At the cry, they overturn the table for a shield and drop to the floor together. But in a room this small, it will probably do no good.

All the Italians brace for death.

In an instant, the exchange of lead scatters blood and leaves casualties on both sides.

ja:
奇襲だった。……恐らく山本中尉は、アンジェロ少尉たちとの交渉で、彼らが言いなりにならないとの感触を得て先手を打ってきたのだ。いや、ひょっとすると、全員で決を採らねばならないように仕向け、集まったところを一網打尽にしようと、初めから狙っていたのかもしれない。六軒島は彼らの島だ。イタリア人を皆殺しにすれば、黄金は五分五分どころか、その全てが日本人のものなのだ。手榴弾が遅れて爆発しないとも限らない。
彼らは廊下へ飛び出る。彼方より銃声が聞こえる。潜水艦ドックの方だ。黄金の山を警備させている兵士たちが襲われているのは明白だ。
en:
An ambush.

...Lieutenant Yamamoto probably sensed during his negotiation with Angelo that the Italians would not do as he said, and struck first.

Or perhaps he had meant from the beginning to make them call a vote, gather them in one place, and wipe them all out.

Rokkenjima is their island. Kill all the Italians, and the Japanese get not half the gold, but all of it.

The grenade might yet explode. They rush into the corridor.

Gunfire sounds in the distance, from the submarine dock. Clearly, the soldiers guarding the pile of gold are under attack.

“Sub-Lieutenant!! Your orders!!”

“We have no choice!! Kill the Japanese!!”

“L-Lieutenant! They can fight!! These men aren't just sailors!”

“Heh heh heh. I see. Good enough to be entrusted with guarding the gold, are they? We have more men. Don't rush. Surround them and kill them!! We're hunting Italians!!”

ja: 連発する発砲音を聞いた時、私はすぐに直感した。あの黄金が荷揚げされた日から、燻っていた何かが、とうとう破裂したのだと直感した。中尉たちが黄金を見る目は、尋常ではなかった。そう、あれは悪魔に魅せられた目だった。イタリア人たちも、重責から心がはちきれそうになっていた。遠い異国の地で、言葉も文字もわからない世界に取り残されたら、おかしくならない方がおかしい。とにかく、何とかしなくてはならないと思い、発砲音の聞こえる方へ走った。……今にして思えば、それはとても愚かしいことだ。それは銃撃戦を意味する音。殺し合いを意味する音。なのに私は丸腰で、まるで喧嘩の仲裁にでも行くようなつもりで、駆けている。……それが如何に愚かしく、この戦時に浮世離れしたものか、すぐに思い知る。
en:
When I heard the repeated shots, I knew at once.

Whatever had been smoldering since the gold was unloaded had finally burst.

There was nothing normal about the way the lieutenant and his men looked at that gold. Yes. Those were the eyes of men bewitched by a devil.

The Italians, too, were near to bursting under the weight of their responsibility. Stranded in a distant foreign land where they could understand neither the speech nor the writing, it would have been strange if they hadn't gone mad.

I had to do something. I ran toward the gunfire.

...Looking back, it was terribly foolish.

Those sounds meant a gun battle. They meant men killing men.

Yet I was running toward them unarmed, as though I intended to break up a quarrel.

...I soon learned how foolish that was. How far removed, in this time of war, from the real world.

en:
He was lying facedown, drenched in blood.

A thick trail of it showed that he had somehow crawled from the room to this spot before dying.

No. He was still twitching. Perhaps he wasn't dead yet. ...But there was no doctor on this island. ...No, even with a doctor— shot so many times, his chest gouged open— how could he possibly be saved...?

I looked into the room he must have crawled from. It was wrecked. Two more blood-soaked Japanese bodies lay inside.

Perhaps he wasn't dead yet. ...But there was no doctor on this island. ...No, even with a doctor— shot so many times, his chest gouged open— how could he possibly be saved...? I looked into the room he must have crawled from. It was wrecked. Two more blood-soaked Japanese bodies lay inside.
rows.jaText: 彼は血で全身を濡らして、うつ伏せに倒れていた。血の跡がべっとりと続き、部屋から何とかここまで這いずってきて、絶命したことが見て取れた。いや、まだ痙攣している。絶命はしていないのかもしれない。……しかし、医者などいないこの島で、……いや、医者がいたとしても、こんな、何発も撃たれて、胸が抉れて、……助かるはずなどあるものか…。這い出てきたに違いない室内を見ると、荒れ果て、他にも２人の日本人の血塗れの死体があった。

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
en: “Ahh, wha...ah... ...D...dead...”
rows.enText: “Ahh, wha...ah... ...D...dead...”

ja: 情けなく尻餅を付き、口を閉じることさえ忘れ、呆然とする……。……思えばそれが、生まれて初めて知る、人の死というものだった。世界中が戦争をしている。洋の東西で、大勢の人が死んでいるこの戦時下でありながらも、……それが初めて直面する人の死だったのだ。
en:
I fell pathetically on my backside and sat there in a stupor, forgetting even to close my mouth...

...That, I realize now, was my first experience of human death.

The whole world was at war. People were dying in great numbers in the East and the West.

Yet in the midst of that war, ...this was the first human death I had ever faced.
rows.enText: I fell pathetically on my backside and sat there in a stupor, forgetting even to close my mouth... ...That, I realize now, was my first experience of human death. The whole world was at war. People were dying in great numbers in the East and the West. Yet in the midst of that war, ...this was the first human death I had ever faced.

ja: 滑稽なものだ。……私は死にたくて軍隊を望んだのではないのか？死にたくて、戦地に送られなかったことを嘆いたのではなかったか？あぁ、なら喜べ、金蔵。これが、私の望んだ死ではないか…！なぜ両手を広げてこう叫べない？　来たれ、偉大なる死よッ、と！！誰かが駆けて来る。同僚だ、日本人だ。田島くんだ。
en:
Absurd.

...Hadn't I wanted to join the military so that I could die? Hadn't I lamented not being sent to the battlefield because I wanted to die?

Then rejoice, Kinzou. This is the death I wanted...!

Why couldn't I open my arms and cry out: Come, great Death!!

Someone came running. A colleague. A Japanese man. Tajima.
rows.enText: Absurd. ...Hadn't I wanted to join the military so that I could die? Hadn't I lamented not being sent to the battlefield because I wanted to die? Then rejoice, Kinzou. This is the death I wanted...! Why couldn't I open my arms and cry out: Come, great Death!! Someone came running. A colleague. A Japanese man. Tajima.

ja: 「にッ、ににッ、にぃッ…！！」
rows.jaText: 「にッ、ににッ、にぃッ…！！」

ja: 顔面を蒼白にしながら、ものすごい形相で駆けて来る。くしゃくしゃに歪んだ酷い顔だった。そしてそれが、きっと自分の顔でもあるのだ。
en:
His face was deathly pale, his features horribly contorted.

And surely that was my own face too.
rows.enText: His face was deathly pale, his features horribly contorted. And surely that was my own face too.
rows.jaText: 顔面を蒼白にしながら、ものすごい形相で駆けて来る。くしゃくしゃに歪んだ酷い顔だった。そしてそれが、きっと自分の顔でもあるのだ。

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「田島くん…、な、何があったんだ……」
en: “Tajima... Wh-what happened...?”
rows.enText: “Tajima... Wh-what happened...?”
rows.jaText: 「田島くん…、な、何があったんだ……」

ja: 「に、逃げろ…。こ、殺、殺されるぅうぅうッ！！」
en: “R-run... Th-they'll k-kill usss!!”
rows.enText: “R-run... Th-they'll k-kill usss!!”
rows.jaText: 「に、逃げろ…。こ、殺、殺されるぅうぅうッ！！」

ja: イタリア語の怒声と共に、田島くんが爆ぜた悲鳴をあげる…。そしてそのまま、腰を落として取っ組みかかってくるかのように、私に飛び込んできた。彼の背中から血が噴き出て、みるみる真っ赤に染まっていく…。
en:
At an angry shout in Italian, a scream burst from Tajima.

Then he sank low and hurled himself at me, as though he were trying to grapple with me.

Blood spurted from his back. It turned red before my eyes...
rows.enText: At an angry shout in Italian, a scream burst from Tajima. Then he sank low and hurled himself at me, as though he were trying to grapple with me. Blood spurted from his back. It turned red before my eyes...
rows.jaText: イタリア語の怒声と共に、田島くんが爆ぜた悲鳴をあげる…。そしてそのまま、腰を落として取っ組みかかってくるかのように、私に飛び込んできた。彼の背中から血が噴き出て、みるみる真っ赤に染まっていく…。

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「田島く、ん……ッ、」
en: “Taji...ma...”
rows.enText: “Taji...ma...”
rows.jaText: 「田島く、ん……ッ、」

ja: 血の泡を吐きながら、………それだけを伝え、絶命する。
en: He spat bloody bubbles. ...Told me only that. And died.
rows.enText: He spat bloody bubbles. ...Told me only that. And died.
rows.jaText: 血の泡を吐きながら、………それだけを伝え、絶命する。

ja: しかし私は、絶命の瞬間を目の当たりにするという衝撃的な出来事には、心を奪われなかった。……生きとし生けるものは、本来、他人の死など関心はないのだ。その唯一の関心は、自分が死ぬかどうかにだけ、割かれるのだ。イタリア人が見せる、銃口の奥底だけが、私の心を奪っていた……。私にもたれかかる田島くんの背中が再び爆ぜる。肉が裂け、血飛沫が飛び散る。その熱い飛沫が私の顔を覆った。すでに身動きも叶わない彼にさらにとどめを？あぁ、私は何と愚かなのか……。この期に及んでまだ、私は直面したるこの惨事を理解できないのか！喜べ、金蔵！！　私が望んだものが、今、初めて与えられたというのに…！！イタリア人はとどめを刺すために撃ったのではない。重なり合って倒れている、この、右代宮金蔵を狙って撃ったのだ。
en:
But the shocking sight of a man dying before my eyes did not capture my attention.

...Living things have no real interest in anyone else's death. Their only interest is whether they themselves will die.

Only the deep black muzzle of the Italian's gun held my attention...

Tajima's back burst again as he lay against me. Flesh tore. Blood sprayed. The hot spray covered my face.

A finishing shot into a man who could no longer move?

Oh, what a fool I was...!

Even now, could I not understand the catastrophe before me?

Rejoice, Kinzou!! What I had wanted had been given to me, for the first time...!!

The Italian had not fired to finish him off. He had fired at Kinzou Ushiromiya, lying tangled up with him.

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
en: “Ah...ah...aaaaah!!!”
rows.enText: “Ah...ah...aaaaah!!!”

ja:
彼の死体を跳ね除け、私は床を掻きながら、転げるように走り出す。床を掻いた時、それだけのことで左手の薬指の爪が剥げた。
どれだけ、人は死に対し、全身全霊で抗うというのか。
en:
I threw the body aside and scrambled over the floor, stumbling into a run.

Merely clawing at the floor tore the nail from my left ring finger.

How utterly a person fights against death, with every part of their being.
rows.enText: I threw the body aside and scrambled over the floor, stumbling into a run. Merely clawing at the floor tore the nail from my left ring finger. How utterly a person fights against death, with every part of their being.

ja:
床を転げ、体を削り取りながら走る。痛かった、熱かった。でも、そんなことはどうでも良かった！後ろからイタリア語の怒鳴り声が何度も聞こえた。それが走り、自分を追ってくるように感じられた。振り返りたくもなかった。だからずっとイタリア人が追ってきているように思えて、どこまでも滅茶苦茶に、ぐちゃぐちゃに逃げた。これが、……死……！！
死にたかったんじゃないのか？嫌だ、死にたくないッ！！どうして？　あんなにも望んだのに？
私はもう、知ってしまった。
生きることの、素晴らしさを。彼女が教えてくれた。ビーチェが教えてくれた。彼女と話している時だけ解放された。違う！
彼女と話して、私は初めて生きたのだ。生まれたのだ！！生きたいッ。生きたい生きたい生きたいッ！！　死にたくない！！生きて彼女と会いたい、今すぐに！！　会わなきゃ死ぬ、殺される！！
en:
I rolled across the floor, running, scraping flesh from my body.

It hurt. It burned. But none of that mattered!

Behind me, I heard shouting in Italian, again and again. It seemed to be running after me, pursuing me.

I didn't want to look back. So I felt the Italian was still chasing me, and ran and ran, wildly, horribly, beyond all reason.

This was...death...!!

Hadn't I wanted to die?

No! I don't want to die!!

Why? I wanted it so much, didn't I?

I knew now.

How wonderful it was to live.

She had taught me. Bice had taught me.

Only when I talked with her was I freed.

No!

By talking with her, I had lived for the first time. I had been born!!

I want to live. I want to live, live, live!! I don't want to die!!

I want to live and see her. Right now!! If I don't see her, I'll die. I'll be killed!!

It seemed to be running after me, pursuing me. I didn't want to look back. So I felt the Italian was still chasing me, and ran and ran, wildly, horribly, beyond all reason. This was...death...!! Hadn't I wanted to die? No! I don't want to die!! Why? I wanted it so much, didn't I? I knew now. How wonderful it was to live. She had taught me. Bice had taught me. Only when I talked with her was I freed. No! By talking with her, I had lived for the first time. I had been born!! I want to live. I want to live, live, live!! I don't want to die!! I want to live and see her. Right now!! If I don't see her, I'll die. I'll be killed!!

ja: ………落ち着け金蔵、……彼女だって殺されるかもしれない…！自分が生きても、彼女が殺されたら、それは同じことなんだ……！！気付けば顔は、涙と鼻水と涎でぐちゃぐちゃに歪んでいた。何かに躓いて転ぶことで、ようやく私はわずかの正気を取り戻す。
en:
...Calm down, Kinzou. ...She might be killed too...!

If I survived and she was killed, it would amount to the same thing...!!

Before I knew it, my face was a twisted mess of tears and snot and drool.

Only when I tripped over something and fell did a little sanity return.
rows.enText: ...Calm down, Kinzou. ...She might be killed too...! If I survived and she was killed, it would amount to the same thing...!! Before I knew it, my face was a twisted mess of tears and snot and drool. Only when I tripped over something and fell did a little sanity return.

ja: 発砲音は、まだ断続的に聞こえる。銃撃戦は続いている。そしてそれは、基地中に広がっている。……ビーチェ。……君は、無事なのか……。彼女を探し、安全な場所に匿おう。……中尉たちは黄金を奪うために、イタリア人たちを皆殺しにするだろう。ビーチェも例外にはなるまい。
en:
Shots still sounded intermittently. The gun battle was continuing, spreading through the entire base.

...Bice. ...Are you safe...?

I would find her and hide her somewhere safe.

...The lieutenant and his men would kill every Italian to seize the gold. Bice would be no exception.
rows.enText: Shots still sounded intermittently. The gun battle was continuing, spreading through the entire base. ...Bice. ...Are you safe...? I would find her and hide her somewhere safe. ...The lieutenant and his men would kill every Italian to seize the gold. Bice would be no exception.

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「ビーチェ……。………ビーチェ…！！」
rows.jaText: 「ビーチェ……。………ビーチェ…！！」

ja: 君に会って私は初めて生きた。生まれた。ならば私は君が死ねば再び死ぬ。右代宮金蔵じゃない、……まったく別の金蔵に、全身の細胞が生まれ変わる感触。……もちろん、再び戻れば、今度こそ撃たれるかもしれない恐怖はある。だが、私はもう、死にたくはないのだ。真の意味で。だから、その恐怖を捻じ曲げることが出来る。
en:
Meeting you, I lived for the first time. I was born.

Then if you die, I die again.

Every cell in my body felt reborn as someone else. ...Not Kinzou Ushiromiya, but an entirely different Kinzou.

...Of course I was afraid that if I went back, this time I might be shot.

But I no longer wanted to die. In the truest sense.

So I could twist that fear to my will.

Every cell in my body felt reborn as someone else. ...Not Kinzou Ushiromiya, but an entirely different Kinzou. ...Of course I was afraid that if I went back, this time I might be shot. But I no longer wanted to die. In the truest sense. So I could twist that fear to my will.

rows.speaker: Kinzou Ushiromiya
ja: 「……ビーチェぇえええぇええ！！」
en: “...Biiiiice!!”
rows.enText: “...Biiiiice!!”
rows.jaText: 「……ビーチェぇえええぇええ！！」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: “ルーベンス！　一体、何が起こってるの？！　この騒ぎは何？！”
en: “Rubens!” Beatrice cries in Italian. “What's happening?! What's all this?!”
rows.enText: “Rubens!” Beatrice cries in Italian. “What's happening?! What's all this?!”
rows.jaText: “ルーベンス！　一体、何が起こってるの？！　この騒ぎは何？！”

ja: “君は知らなくていい。そこにじっと隠れていろ。同胞が呼び掛けるまで出てくるんじゃない！”「イタリア人の声が聞こえたッ！！　そこにいるぞ！！」“くそったれ、東洋人め！！”
en:
“You don't need to know. Stay hidden there. Don't come out until one of us calls for you!”

“I heard an Italian voice!! They're in there!!”

“Damn you Asians!!”
rows.enText: “You don't need to know. Stay hidden there. Don't come out until one of us calls for you!” “I heard an Italian voice!! They're in there!!” “Damn you Asians!!”
rows.jaText: “君は知らなくていい。そこにじっと隠れていろ。同胞が呼び掛けるまで出てくるんじゃない！”「イタリア人の声が聞こえたッ！！　そこにいるぞ！！」“くそったれ、東洋人め！！”

ja: ルーベンスはベアトリーチェを背中で庇い、ベレッタＭ１９３４の９ｍｍ弾を正確に１発ずつ、飛び込んできた２人に撃ち込む。しかし彼らも九四式自動拳銃の８ｍｍ弾を正確に１発、ルーベンスの胸に撃ち込む。銃を撃ち合った３人は、３人がそれぞれに銃弾を胸に受けて、もがきながら倒れる。
en:
Rubens shields Beatrice with his back. With his Beretta M1934, he puts one well-aimed 9mm bullet into each of the two men charging in.

But they, too, put one well-aimed 8mm bullet from a Type 94 pistol into his chest.

All three men have taken bullets in the chest. All three fall, writhing.

But they, too, put one well-aimed 8mm bullet from a Type 94 pistol into his chest. All three men have taken bullets in the chest. All three fall, writhing.

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: “し、しっかりしてッ！！　ルーベンス！！”
en: “Hold on!! Rubens!!”
rows.enText: “Hold on!! Rubens!!”
rows.jaText: “し、しっかりしてッ！！　ルーベンス！！”

ja: “……地上へ逃げろ…。森の中へ隠れ……、……ゴホゴホッ！！　グッ……”
en: “...Get aboveground... Hide in the forest... ...Cough! Cough! ...Ghh...”
rows.enText: “...Get aboveground... Hide in the forest... ...Cough! Cough! ...Ghh...”
rows.jaText: “……地上へ逃げろ…。森の中へ隠れ……、……ゴホゴホッ！！　グッ……”

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: “ルーベーンス！！！”
en: “Ruuubens!!!”
rows.enText: “Ruuubens!!!”
rows.jaText: “ルーベーンス！！！”

ja: 「……くっくっく、おやおや。賑やかではないか」
en: “...Heh heh heh. Well, well. Quite a commotion.”
rows.enText: “...Heh heh heh. Well, well. Quite a commotion.”
rows.jaText: 「……くっくっく、おやおや。賑やかではないか」

ja: さらに現れたのは、……日本人たちの指揮官、山本だった。３人が殺し合う銃声を轟かせたのだ。さらにその上、ベアトリーチェの叫びがあっては、気取られても不思議はない。
en:
Another man has arrived: ...Yamamoto, commander of the Japanese.

The gunfire as three men killed one another was loud enough. With Beatrice's cries on top of it, it is hardly surprising he noticed them.

ja: 「こんなことなら、最初からこの女を人質に取ればよかった。クソ、忌々しい連中だ！」
en: “I should have taken this woman hostage from the start. Shit. Miserable bastards!”

en: Yamamoto spits. In that instant, Beatrice snatches up Rubens's gun.

ja: 「躊躇なく銃を拾おうとするとは！　イタリア女は実に物騒だッ！　クソ、二人掛りでしくじりやがって…！！」
en: “Picking up a gun without the slightest hesitation! Italian women are dangerous indeed! Shit. Two of you, and you still botched it...!!”
rows.enText: “Picking up a gun without the slightest hesitation! Italian women are dangerous indeed! Shit. Two of you, and you still botched it...!!”

ja: 足元に転がり、苦しそうに呻いて最期の時を待つ二人に、憎々しげにそう言い放つ。
en: He spits the words venomously at the two men lying at his feet, groaning in agony as they await death.

ja: しかし、無理もないことだった。そしてそれは、ここの撃ち合いだけではない。この、狭く入り組んだ壕内では、ほとんどが出会い頭となる。互いに銃弾を無闇やたらに撃ち込み合えば、転がる骸は二つになる。だから、人の気配さえ感じたら直ちに引き金を引いた方が早い。それが唯一、自分の胸に鉛弾を喰らわない生き残りの方法だ。そんなだから、日本人もイタリア人も、異邦人を容赦なく殺したし、時に出会い頭の同胞にさえ引き金を引いた。そんな中に、何事か何事かと、突然の騒ぎに駆けつけた大勢の日本人たちは次々に巻き込まれていった。相手が銃を持っていようと持っていまいと関係ない。自分が生きるために自分以外の人影に対し、反射的に引き金を引く。そんな殺人劇が、基地内を飲み込んでいった……。潜水艦ドックでは激しい銃撃戦が。そして基地内では狩猟のような惨劇が繰り広げられた。軍属の非戦闘員のほとんどは、何事かもわからない内に撃ち殺された。イタリア人は確かに精兵揃いだったが、少しずつ犠牲者を増やしていった。基地内のそこかしこに、血塗れの死体がごろごろと横たわった……。最初は、少なくとも彼らなりに意味のある銃撃戦だったかもしれない。しかし次第に、彼らの感覚は麻痺し、理解できぬ異邦人は全て殺せという、人類が戦争を起こす理由の、最も根源的なものにすり替わっていった…。自分に理解できない言葉を聞けば、構わず引き金を引いた。異邦人の悲鳴はもはや、人型のケモノのそれと同じに聞こえた。異国の言葉の命乞いなど、理解も出来ないのだから。だからそれはもうとっくに、ただの殺人劇と成り果てていたのだ……。
en:
But it could hardly be helped. And not only in this particular exchange of gunfire.

In these cramped, tangled tunnels, almost every encounter comes without warning. If both men fire indiscriminately into each other, there will be two bodies on the floor.

So the instant you sense another person, it is faster to pull the trigger. The only way to survive without taking lead in your own chest.

Both Japanese and Italians killed foreigners without mercy, and sometimes pulled the trigger on their own comrades when they crossed paths.

Many Japanese men rushed toward the sudden uproar to see what was happening. One by one, they were caught in it.

Whether the other person had a gun made no difference. To save your own life, you fired reflexively at every figure but your own.

That murderous drama swallowed the base...

At the submarine dock, a fierce gun battle. Inside the base, an atrocity more like a hunt.

Most civilian personnel were shot dead before they understood what was happening.

The Italians were indeed elite soldiers, but their casualties mounted little by little.

Blood-soaked bodies lay everywhere throughout the base...

At first, perhaps the gun battle had some meaning, at least to those fighting it.

But as their senses grew numb, it became something else: kill every foreigner you cannot understand. The most fundamental of humanity's reasons for making war...

Hear a language you cannot understand, and pull the trigger without hesitation. The foreigners' screams came to sound like those of beasts in human shape.

After all, they could not understand a plea for life in a foreign tongue.

So it had long since become nothing more than a murderous drama...

ja: そうして死者の数が生きた人間を上回り、……次第に基地内は静寂を取り戻していった。荒涼とした風の音が聞こえ、全ての人間が死に絶えたかと思った頃に、唐突に悲鳴が聞こえては、乾いた銃声が、まだ惨劇が終わっていないことを思い出させる。そんなことが、何度も繰り返し、………やがて、本当の静寂を迎えた。……黄金に惑わされた者たちの、哀れな最期だった。イタリア人たちの指揮官、アンジェロは、何とか生き残っていた。出くわすのは、……敵と、味方の、死体だけ。基地内はシンと静まりかえっている。迂闊に大声を出せば、物影から撃たれるかもしれない。……だからこうして息を殺しながら、残敵を探して、豹のように徘徊する…。生きた者の姿も、気配も、何もない。……この基地にいる全ての人間がもう、死に絶えたかもしれない。
en:
The dead outnumbered the living. ...Little by little, silence returned to the base.

The bleak wind would be audible, and it would seem everyone had died. Then a sudden scream, a dry gunshot, would remind them that the atrocity was not over.

It happened again and again.

...And at last, true silence came.

...A pitiful end for those beguiled by gold.

Angelo, commander of the Italians, has somehow survived.

He encounters only bodies. ...Enemies and friends.

The base is deathly still. A careless shout might draw fire from the shadows.

...So he prowls like a leopard, holding his breath, seeking the remaining enemy.

There is no living figure. No sign of life. ...Perhaps every person in this base is already dead.

ja: “……日本人め、おのれ……”
en: “...Damn you Japanese...”
rows.enText: “...Damn you Japanese...”
rows.jaText: “……日本人め、おのれ……”

ja:
日本人が先に仕掛けて来たが、あの時、我々もまた、日本人を殺すことを相談していた。彼らは軍人として、機先を制しただけのことだ。
だから、とりあえず今日に、感謝することにした。迎えの船が来たところで、自分たちにはもう名誉など与えられはしない。死んだ戦友たちに顔向け出来ない、哀れな任務失敗を思い知るだけ。この極東の地で銃を抱いて死ねるのは、………軍人として本懐かもしれないのだ。
en:
The Japanese had attacked first. But at that very moment, he and his men had been discussing killing them too. As soldiers, the Japanese had simply beaten them to it.

So for now, he decides to be grateful for this day.

Even if the ship comes to collect them, no honor awaits. Only the realization of a pitiful failure, unable to face their dead comrades.

To die in this Far Eastern land with a gun in his arms ...might be a soldier's true fulfillment.

ja:
曲がり角の向こうに、足を引き摺る音を聞き、耳をそばだてる。………負傷して、足を引き摺っているのか？　先に気配を気取れたのは、勝機。もうこの段階において、捕虜を取る意味はない。
むしろ、全ての日本人を排除すべきだ。曲がり角より飛び出して、素早く相手を確認し、……日本人だったら撃つ。それだけのことだ。自分はずっと足音を殺していた。こちらは気取られていないはず。引き摺る足音が、充分な間合いまで近付いてきてから、アンジェロは身を乗り出し、銃を構える。そんな彼を迎えたのは、イタリア語だった。
en:
He hears a dragging footstep around a corner and listens hard.

...A wounded man, dragging a leg? Sensing him first is an opportunity.

There is no point taking prisoners anymore. Better to eliminate every Japanese man.

Step around the corner, identify the man quickly, ...and shoot if he's Japanese. That is all.

Angelo has kept his own footsteps silent. He should not have been detected.

Once the dragging footsteps are close enough, he leans around the corner and raises his gun.

What greets him is Italian.

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: “に、逃げて……”
en: “R-run...”
rows.enText: “R-run...”
rows.jaText: “に、逃げて……”

ja: “……？！　き、貴様……！！”「くっくっく、貴様を探していたぞ、アンジェロ少尉…。これで全員だな。俺はしっかり、貴様らの死体を数えて回ってたんだからな…！！」
en:
“...?! Y-you...!!”

“Heh heh heh. I've been looking for you, Sub-Lieutenant Angelo... That makes all of you. I've been counting your bodies carefully...!!”

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: “しッ、しっかりして！！　アンジェロ少尉！”
en: “Hold on!! Sub-Lieutenant Angelo!”
rows.enText: “Hold on!! Sub-Lieutenant Angelo!”
rows.jaText: “しッ、しっかりして！！　アンジェロ少尉！”

ja: アンジェロは胸から、こぽりと血が溢れ出し、……銃を落とす音、膝を落とす音に続き、どさりと床に崩れ落ちる音を聞かせ、……動かなくなった。山本の銃の腕は決していい方ではない。しかし、アンジェロが充分に間合いを詰めてから飛び出してくれたので、当てることが出来た。銃身の短い拳銃を片手で構え、……女を人質に取りながらでも、当てることが出来た。
en:
Blood wells from Angelo's chest.

...The sound of a gun dropping. Then his knees striking the floor. Then the heavy thud of his body.

...He does not move again.

Yamamoto is by no means a good shot. But Angelo waited until they were close before stepping out, putting himself within easy range.

Even with a short-barreled pistol in one hand. ...Even with a woman held hostage.

ja: 「それにしても、我が六軒島守備隊の情けないことよ！　まさか私以外は全員死んだのではあるまいな？！　やれやれクズどもめ！」
en: “But what a disgrace my Rokkenjima garrison is! Surely they haven't all died and left only me?! Useless scum!”
rows.enText: “But what a disgrace my Rokkenjima garrison is! Surely they haven't all died and left only me?! Useless scum!”
rows.jaText: 「それにしても、我が六軒島守備隊の情けないことよ！　まさか私以外は全員死んだのではあるまいな？！　やれやれクズどもめ！」

rows.speaker: Beatrice
ja: “女を楯に取らなきゃ戦えない、人でなし！！　離してッ！”
en: “You monster! You can't fight without a woman for a shield!! Let me go!”
rows.enText: “You monster! You can't fight without a woman for a shield!! Let me go!”
rows.jaText: “女を楯に取らなきゃ戦えない、人でなし！！　離してッ！”

ja: 「静かにしろ！　イタリア女は実に騒がしい。大人しくしてれば、命までは取らんというのにッ。くっくっく！」
en: “Be quiet! Italian women are so noisy. Behave yourself and I won't kill you. Heh heh heh!”
rows.enText: “Be quiet! Italian women are so noisy. Behave yourself and I won't kill you. Heh heh heh!”
rows.jaText: 「静かにしろ！　イタリア女は実に騒がしい。大人しくしてれば、命までは取らんというのにッ。くっくっく！」

ja: それは、彼自身が苦笑いしてしまうほどの嘘だ。イタリア人たちは敵に内通したスパイで、銃撃戦になり、守備隊共々全滅した。そういう筋書きにしたい山本にとって、イタリア人生存者は不都合なのだ。もはや黄金の山を丸ごと手に入れることは出来ないが、自分で持ち運べる程度の、インゴット数本をくすねることは出来るはず。そしてそれだけでも、十分な大金になるはず。
en:
It is such a lie that even he has to give a wry laugh.

The Italians were spies in league with the enemy. A gun battle broke out, and they were wiped out together with the garrison.

That is the story Yamamoto wants to tell. A surviving Italian is inconvenient.

He can no longer take the entire mountain of gold. But he should be able to steal a few ingots, as much as he can carry himself.

And that alone should be a considerable fortune.

en: Suddenly, Beatrice throws her head back hard. It smashes into the bridge of Yamamoto's nose.
